questions.question_text: A Wyoming landlord asks what the maximum security deposit is under state law. The correct answer is:
questions.correct_answer: There is no statutory maximum in Wyoming
distractors: One month's rent for unfurnished units
Two months' rent for all rental units
Three months' rent for furnished units
questions.explanation: Wyoming does not impose a statutory cap on security deposit amounts. This is one of several provisions that make Wyoming considered landlord-friendly. The amount is left to negotiation between landlord and tenant.

questions.question_text: A tenant's lease ends March 1 and the tenant provides a forwarding address on March 5. There is no damage to the unit. By when must the landlord return the security deposit?
questions.correct_answer: March 31, which is 30 days after lease termination
distractors: March 20, which is 15 days after the address
April 4, which is 30 days after the address
March 15, which is 14 days after termination
questions.explanation: Under W.S. 1-21-1208(a) the landlord must deliver or mail the deposit balance and a written itemization within 30 days after termination of the rental agreement OR within 15 days after receipt of the renter's new mailing address, whichever is LATER. Thirty days from March 1 is March 31; 15 days from March 5 is March 20. March 31 is later, so March 31 applies. (Had the unit been damaged, the same subsection would extend the period by another 30 days.)

questions.question_text: A tenant's lease ends June 1, the unit is undamaged, but the tenant does not provide a forwarding address until July 1. When is the deposit due?
questions.correct_answer: July 16, which is 15 days after the address
distractors: July 1, which is 30 days after termination
June 15, which is 14 days after termination
July 31, which is 30 days after the address
questions.explanation: W.S. 1-21-1208(a) sets the deadline at 30 days after termination of the rental agreement OR 15 days after receipt of the renter's new mailing address, whichever is LATER. Thirty days from June 1 is July 1, but 15 days from July 1 is July 16. July 16 is later, so that is the deadline. The same subsection requires the renter to supply the new address within 30 days of termination, and extends the landlord's deadline by another 30 days if the unit is damaged.

questions.question_text: A landlord deducts $400 from a $1,200 security deposit for carpet damage. What must the landlord provide to the tenant?
questions.correct_answer: An itemized list of the deductions
distractors: Only the remaining $800 with no explanation
Receipts for the actual repair work completed
A signed statement from the property manager
questions.explanation: W.S. 1-21-1208(a) requires the owner to deliver or mail the deposit balance together with a WRITTEN itemization of any deductions and the reasons for them. Repair receipts are good practice but are not required by statute. Because there is damage to the unit here, the same subsection extends the normal return deadline by an additional 30 days. If the owner unreasonably fails to comply, W.S. 1-21-1208(c) lets the renter recover the full deposit plus court costs.

questions.question_text: A Wyoming tenant asks their landlord what interest rate applies to the security deposit. The landlord should respond:
questions.correct_answer: Wyoming does not require interest on deposits
distractors: Interest accrues at the prevailing bank rate
Two percent per year on the total deposit
The rate is set annually by WREC
questions.explanation: Wyoming has no statutory requirement for landlords to pay interest on security deposits. This is another landlord-friendly provision. Some other states do require interest, but Wyoming does not.

questions.question_text: A Wyoming tenant is three days behind on rent. The landlord wants to begin eviction. What notice is required?
questions.correct_answer: A 3-day written notice to quit the premises
distractors: A 5-day written notice to quit the premises
A 10-day written notice to vacate
A 14-day notice to cure the default
questions.explanation: Two separate 3-day periods apply. W.S. 1-21-1002(a)(i) allows a forcible entry and detainer action only 'after a failure to pay rent for three (3) days after it is due.' W.S. 1-21-1003 then requires the landlord to 'notify the adverse party to leave the premises,' in writing, 'at least three (3) days before commencing the action.' Wyoming's statutory notice is a notice to QUIT, not a statutory pay-or-quit — the Judicial Branch form is titled 'Notice to Quit Premises' — although paying the rent before the FED is filed eliminates the grounds for it.

questions.question_text: A tenant on a month-to-month lease in Wyoming has not violated any terms and the lease is silent on termination. How much notice should the landlord give to terminate?
distractors: 60 days written notice
3 days written notice
No notice is required for month-to-month
questions.explanation: No Wyoming statute fixes a notice period for ending a periodic tenancy — the Residential Rental Property Act and the forcible entry and detainer article are both silent. Under common law, and per Wyoming Judicial Branch guidance, a month-to-month tenancy is ended on notice of one full rental period, i.e. a full month's (30 days') notice, unless the rental agreement provides otherwise. If the tenant then holds over, the landlord must STILL serve the 3-day notice to quit required by W.S. 1-21-1003 before filing a forcible entry and detainer action under W.S. 1-21-1002(a)(i).

questions.question_text: A tenant violates a lease term by keeping an unauthorized pet. What notice period applies in Wyoming?
distractors: 10 days to cure the violation
30 days written notice to vacate
7 days to remedy or vacate
questions.explanation: W.S. 1-21-1002(a)(vi) allows a forcible entry and detainer action 'against renters in violation of any terms imposed under W.S. 1-21-1204 or 1-21-1205.' An unauthorized pet breaches W.S. 1-21-1204(a)(vii), which requires the renter to 'comply with all lawful requirements of the rental agreement.' W.S. 1-21-1003 then requires written notice to leave the premises served at least 3 days before the action is filed — the same 3 days as for nonpayment. Note this is a notice to QUIT, not a cure period: Wyoming gives no statutory right to fix the violation and stay.

questions.question_text: A Casper landlord asks how much Wyoming law lets him raise the rent at renewal. The correct answer is:
questions.correct_answer: No Wyoming statute limits residential rent increases
distractors: Increases are capped at five percent per year
WREC sets the maximum annual increase
Increases above ten percent require 90 days notice
questions.explanation: Wyoming has no rent control or rent stabilization law and no statutory cap on rent increases. The Residential Rental Property Act, W.S. 1-21-1201 through 1-21-1211, governs habitability, security deposits, abandoned property and remedies, but is silent on rent amounts, and no other Wyoming statute regulates residential rent. No Wyoming municipality has adopted a rent control ordinance. The amount and timing of any increase are governed by the rental agreement.

questions.question_text: A tenant's furnace fails in January. Under the Wyoming Residential Rental Property Act, the landlord must:
questions.correct_answer: Maintain operational heating and act within a reasonable time after written notice
distractors: Complete the repair within 48 hours or forfeit the rent
Do nothing, because Wyoming imposes no habitability duty
Permit the tenant to repair the furnace and deduct the cost from rent
questions.explanation: Wyoming's habitability duty is statutory, not an implied warranty. W.S. 1-21-1202(a) requires every residential rental unit to have 'operational electrical, heating and plumbing, with hot and cold running water,' and W.S. 1-21-1203(a)(iii) requires the owner to maintain heating. Under W.S. 1-21-1203(b) a renter who is current on rent gives the owner WRITTEN notice specifying the requested remedy; within a reasonable time the owner must either begin corrective action or dispute the claim in writing. Wyoming sets no fixed emergency-repair deadline and the Act contains no repair-and-deduct remedy: the renter's next step is the 'notice to repair or correct condition' under W.S. 1-21-1206(b), which warns that court action follows if the owner does not begin corrective action within 3 days.
